transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Thank you for seeing me. I decided to come in because I just don’t feel any interest in the community projects and hobbies that used to mean everything to me. It feels like I've completely lost my connection to the things that used to give my life purpose.
Have you ever had a similar period of depression or loss of interest like this before, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before. This is the first time in my life I've felt so completely disconnected, and it really only started after that terrible accident. Before that, I was always very active and happy.
Since this started, have you also been feeling down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or having changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration?

Yes, I constantly carry this heavy mix of guilt and dread, like a dark cloud that makes it impossible to feel happy or at ease anymore. My concentration has also been terrible—I often lose my train of thought mid-conversation and struggle to make simple daily decisions, like what to cook for dinner. It's just a constant, wearying struggle.
How long have these symptoms of low mood, loss of interest, guilt, and poor concentration been going on continuously?
They've been going on continuously for a little over two years now, ever since that terrible accident at the crosswalk. They really haven't let up at all since then.
Since the accident, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or do you try to avoid reminders of it because they bring up intense distress?

Yes, if I hear tires screech or see a truck, I'm right back on that corner watching that boy get hit, which makes me feel completely sick and shaky. I go the long way around town to avoid that intersection, and I immediately shut down or change the subject if anyone brings up the accident because it makes my chest tighten.
Since the accident, do you also feel constantly on edge or easily startled, have trouble sleeping because of it, or find yourself being unusually watchful for danger?

Yes, I am constantly on edge and incredibly watchful now. I watch cars like a hawk and tense up at every loud engine rev, always checking the street before stepping off the curb. Even when I'm just sitting in a café, I have to face the door so I can keep an eye on everything around me.

Did these symptoms begin after the accident and include intrusive memories, avoidance, and feeling constantly on edge, or did they start for no clear reason and persist most of the day nearly every day?

These symptoms absolutely started right after that tragic accident two years ago, rather than for no reason. Ever since that day, I constantly feel on edge watching cars, relive the crash when I hear screeching tires, and go completely out of my way to avoid that intersection.
Have you had any periods of feeling emotionally numb or detached from other people, or any sudden outbursts of anger or irritability since the accident?

Yes, I feel terribly detached, like I'm behind a pane of glass watching everyone at church or the senior center without being able to connect. I've also been very irritable and snap at people over tiny things, like a friend being slightly late, which makes me feel deeply ashamed afterward.
Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to work, manage daily tasks, or maintain relationships, and if so how much have they interfered?

Yes, they have completely taken over my life and disrupted everything. I've stopped leading my walking tours, dropped out of my church and senior center activities, and even cut back on driving. My world has shrunk to mostly sitting at home alone, and I've lost all the structure and meaning I used to have.
Since the accident and these symptoms started, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or any thoughts of hurting yourself?

I don't have active plans to hurt myself, but on nights when the memories won't quiet down, I drink more wine than I should and drive too fast on back roads, thinking, "Who cares what happens to me anyway." Deep down, I know that's not how I really feel, but in those moments, I feel a reckless disregard for my own safety.
Did your symptoms begin only after the accident and stay tied to reminders of it, or did they start independently of the accident and persist most of the day nearly every day?

Everything definitely started right after the accident two years ago and hasn't let up since. It is really a mix of both: specific reminders like screeching tires trigger those sudden, intense reactions, but the heavy cloud of guilt, dread, and loss of interest is constant and stays with me almost all day, every single day.
Did these problems begin only after the accident and get triggered by reminders of it, or did they start without any clear trigger and persist most of the day nearly every day?

They definitely started right after the accident and have been with me ever since. It is really a mix of both, because while specific reminders like screeching tires trigger those intense panic reactions, I also carry a heavy cloud of guilt and dread that stays with me almost every single day.

Have your symptoms been mainly tied to the accident and reminders of it, or have you also had a separate period of low mood and loss of interest that lasted at least two weeks without being related to the trauma?

No, I haven't had any separate periods like that at all. Everything—the low mood, the loss of interest, and the constant distress—started directly after the accident and has been ongoing ever since. Before that day, I never struggled with anything like this.
Have your symptoms been present for less than a month after the accident, or have they continued for more than a month?
They have been present for much longer than a month. These symptoms have been going on continuously for over two years, ever since the accident occurred, and they really haven't let up at all.
Did your symptoms start within a month after the accident and stay tied to reminders of it, or did they begin much later or without a clear link to the trauma?

Yes, they started almost immediately after that terrible night and have been hanging over me ever since. They are very much tied to reminders, like hearing tires screech, seeing a truck near a crosswalk, or even just thinking about that intersection.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder: symptoms began immediately after a clearly identified traumatic accident, have persisted for over two years, and include intrusive re-experiencing (triggered memories/flashback-like reactions), avoidance of reminders, persistent hypervigilance/startle, emotional detachment, irritability, guilt/dread, and marked functional impairment. A separate independent major depressive episode was denied, making primary depressive disorder less likely; adjustment disorder is less likely given the severity, duration, and full PTSD symptom cluster.
